headline: Tesla says its Austin fleet of driverless Cybercab taxis has grown eightfold in a month to more than 300, and a senior executive says Dallas is next.
score_reason: Pool score 7 lowered one point: the fleet size is Tesla's own claim, a community tracker saw only 105 Cybercabs in service, and a federal safety review is open.
importance_line: Riders in Austin may see more driverless Tesla taxis and Dallas may follow, but the 300-plus count is Tesla's own, a community tracker saw roughly a third of that in service, and the federal safety review is not finished.
summary: Teslarati reports that Tesla's Robotaxi account on X said on 10 October that more than 300 Cybercab driverless taxis now serve Austin, an eightfold rise in 30 days and the first official fleet count Tesla has given, while Ashok Elluswamy, Tesla's head of AI software, wrote "Dallas soon". The figure is Tesla's own: a community tracker, whose counts can lag, listed only 105 Cybercabs in service on Saturday, Texas records show 319 registered, and the US safety regulator NHTSA wants Tesla's sworn answers by 30 October on whether the Cybercab meets federal safety standards.
notes: Read from the pre-fetched full text. Event date 10 Oct 2026. Dallas is an executive's post, not a formal launch announcement.
